Not entirely sure what you mean, but I don't think who you targeted should matter. Mr. Fixer is great against The Rat, because all of that self damage and damage to other heroes gets redirected to The Rat (cancel that first attack, then hit all non-hero targets). If it mattered who you hit, that would never work. If you say that the "next damage" buff should apply to every target, then so should Bloody Knuckles.

I'm assuming you're taking Driving Mantis into account here? If so, it's not exactly the same scenario because you're allowed to redirect damage when he is damaging himself.

 

Mr. Fixer hits himself with Bloody Knuckles in play, base attack 1 damage, +2 for Bloody Knuckles, then another +2 for Bloody Knuckles. Now, that same damge should then apply to all other targets as the final damage modifications, but it isn't.

I agree that's how it SHOULD work. I'm still trying to make sense of Christopher's thought process though, and based on how his answer was worded, he seemed to take issue with the fact that Jack Hammer has a special damage order than usual. Here's what specifically doesn't make sense to me in the Bloody Knuckles ruling: he adds "No, it is an automatic effect, so you will read strike as "do all non-hero targets 1 melee damage" or any other damage he can do pretty much."

See that last part there? It implies modifiers can occur across the board, but they're specific to the conditions in which the damage was applied. Jack Handle shouldn't care if it was only applicable to the first instance or not, it just spreads damage to everything evenly. Because it says "the same amount of damage

A) We reevaluate all modifications, and start fresh with new targets (just like redirections). In this case, only the first one hit will get the buff.

Here's where I disagree, and here's why: Jack Handle specifically deals the same damage as the first target received. In my mind, you share the same window of opportunity with two cards (I'll use Parse as an example): Critical Multiplier and Jack Handle. Critical Multiplier's damage is applied, and since it has been ruled that you can apply cards in the desired order, you can then say that Jack Handle would deal 1+X damage, before the first target is even hit.

B) We only take some of the modifications. Because of the Bloody Knuckles ruling, we know that damage modifications from the defender do not matter. So, even though we needed to calculate the modifications to see if any hp was reduced in order to see if we can hit other targets, we are now going to ignore those modifications, but keep others. Honestly, this is a stretch, and if true, the word "that" is one amazing word. It doesn't actually mean "that whole damage," but only "some of that damage."

Again, it's about how cards are worded. Jack Handle applies before damage is dealt, because of the "would deal" phrase. Errata could make this whole mess go away, or perhaps we can ask Christopher to re-evaluate the interactions.

Here's my best guess, after reading and interpreting these phrases for a good hour. The way I think Christopher intended Jack Handle to work is to ignore modifiers before determining applicable damage. In which case, there is a confliction with order of operations of damage. This is how I believe it SHOULD go:

  1. Determine damage type

  2. Determine if damage can be dealt (the condition of Jack Handle)

  3. Identify and apply all modifiers to dealing (the modifiers applied afterwards)

  4. Determine if damaged is dealt, and reduce hp

  5. Apply effects based on damage being dealt

But since all targets can't take the same damage as Mr. Fixer, this leads me to believe modifiers are a case-by-case basis. In which case it's indeed an errata issue. And Jack Handle should read:

Whenever Mr. Fixer would deal Damage to a Target, he also deals Damage to all non-Hero targets.
When this card enters play, return any other Tool cards in play to your hand.

"That much damage" is the problem phrase here.

It's not refering to the specific amount of damage, but rather the instance of damage itself that is going to be modified. There is no notion of "snapshoting" stats in SotM (which is something I brought up in another discussion somewhere). The closest thing to a snapshot mechanic is the "Use X were X = Y" wording, which is specifically not used with Fixer's weapons.

>
“jack handle”
the first paragraph on this card reads “whenever mr. this may cause an interesting twist if mr. Fixer has a card like plague rat’s “infection” card on him, which reads in part “at the start of that hero’s turn, they deal themselves 1 irreducible toxic damage”. in this case, the 1 irreducible toxic damage he would do to himself get cancelled and is replaced by the same amount/type of damage to all non-hero targets. this not only makes mr. fixer immune to the damage he would normally cause himself when under the influence of an “infection” card, but the damage he deals out to all non-hero targets is irreducible just like the original damage he would have dealt.
 
lastly, what exactly does “that much damage” mean? it means that whatever amount of damage was dealt after taking into account all modifiers is what is dealt to all non-hero cards, with no further modification. so, If mr. Fixer would deal 1 damage plus 2 due to modifiers, 3 damage is how much is done
to all non-hero targets, not the 3 plus another 2. note that using “jack handle” isn’t a separate step in an attack for mr. fixer. it is an automatic effect which occurs with every attack.
 
So, basically, you snapshot the original damage and then apply it.

Pre-Parse Fixer was the best way to beat heavy armor, with Tiger and Crane.  His redirection is the most persistant in the game until Writhe, Grease Gun is awesome, and Salvage Yard is insanely good.

Fixer has so many ways to have a big impact on the game:

Hoist chain + overdrive/charge to take 2 away from a target's damage.

Tire Iron giving you a persistent sucker punch effect that also deals damage.

Jackhandle/crowbars giving a boost when something causes you to deal damage to yourself or others.

Salvage yard explaoiting any hero ability that allows them to discard/destroy equipment for any effect.  (Haka, Bunker, Expat, KNYFE, Nightmist, Omnitron-X, Argent Adept all can exploit this effect).

 

The complaints I hear about Fixer usually go one of these routes:

1.  We don't play advanced:  If you don't play advanced Fixer loses a ton of value.  Most non-advanced games are a damage race, and Fixer doesn't win those.

2.  I wanted a certain setup and got other cards.  A lot of times a case where the player needs to be more flexible, but also a lot of times you get his situationally awesome cards in the wrong situation.

3.  There was a very specific situation that Fixer could have solved if I had the right cards:  This is always disappointing, but it happens for anyone, it is just that Fixer has ways to solve problems that other heroes can't solve, so it stands out more.

4.  Fixer is a damage dealer that doesn't deal very good damage.  This is because Fixer is a low build damage dealer, but moreso he is a utility hero that uses his attacks to help the team in ways other than just the number of health he knocks off the target.

posts.cooked:
I think the thing I find frustrating in my experience with Fixer is the number of times people talk about a specific villain being compromised by two to three specific cards in Fixer's arsenal when his only method of card accelleration/deck searching is Meditation and Tool Box (both fine cards).  But finding a specific Tool in his deck for a specific situation is something I have trouble with.

I completely understand the utility Fixer brings to the table.  I get the amazing things he can pull off.

I find that his deck doesn't allow him to get those combinations when he needs them.

I think that's why I'm so drawn to Dark Watch Fixer.  I don't experience as much of an issue with finding the right card combinations.  Riveting Crane can be used by itself with no need for a Charge or a damage buffing Tool!  I can benefit from Bloody Knuckles without taking all of that added damage!  The blown-up Equipment or Ongoing seems to be relatively easy to deal with by witholding Bitter Strike during key moments when the heroes can afford some set-up.  If that isn't an option then he can continue to break most of his stuff and continue fueling it through the sheer number of Tools/Styles he has in his deck.

I'm not trying to argue one version "sucks" or the other "fixes" the character, but I've just seen somewhat of a disconnect between Fixer afficionados and people who just can't get into Fixer.  I had a friend who nearly always had a great starting hand with Expatriette and he had very little context for the complaints many have levied against her for her lack of draw accelleration.  He always had exactly what he needed to effectively fight a baddie.  That's just not something that I've experienced.  When I rarely get that perfect hand?  Oh man, I have a blast!

My point is that with Fixer some folks seem to think that he sucks because they don't get his nuance, but others will assume frustrated players just "don't get it" when what they're really not getting are the appropriate cards to get the great combos Fixer can pull off.  And it's really disheartening to hear "Well you should have brought TL;DR Tachyon/Anthony Drake Argent Adept/Vanilla Visionary/The Scholar to accellerate his plays and/or draws."

I'm really excited to see what we learn from Fixer in the RC expansion for the video game, because I've felt that a lot of the things people have praised about Fixer in the past have been reappropriated to other heroes (Parse) or just outright ruled as an incorrect understanding of how the game plays (Dual Crowbars having damage be exactly the same but still being lowered if there is damage reduction or prevention, not getting double buffed by Bloody Knuckles when he targets himself with Jack Handle, etc.).

I'm not trying to change any minds here.  Well...actually I'm totally trying to get people who assume Fixer sucks to try him out a few more times and folks who assume that anyone who doesn't like Fixer can't comprehend his utility to figure out what someone's issue with this character is before assuming it stems from ignorance.  I'm just happy DW Fixer was made because I like having the opportunity for more players to enjoy this game with all of the heroes.

It's difficult to prescribe a mode of play, telling people what cards they should play and when, because it's not that sort of game. I don't believe that there is ever a right or best move that you can make due to the large number of moving parts.

Reckless:

but I don't really understand why everyone brings up his combos with specific cards against specific villains being rewarding if the whole point of Fixer is to appreciate the hand fate gave you and stuff any frustrations you may have with it.

Are you perhaps looking at post about Mister Fixer's best combos against certain villains? You can find that with any hero. Such as Legacy versus Chairman: Lead From the Front, 2 Next Evolutions, and The Legacy Ring. The Visionary versus Citizen Dawn: Precognition, Brain Burn, and Suggestion.

While these are examples of how well a good hand can shut down some villains, it is not the only thing they are capable of doing to defeat said villains.

A popular Mister Fixer one is Jack Handle, Dual Crowbars, and/or Driving Mantis against Plague Rat. While those are probably the best cards Mister Fixer can bring to the table against Plague Rat, they are far from his only cards that can be usable against him.  Hoist Chain is good just to reduce some of Plague Rat's damage, even better with Overdrive and/or Charge, as it'll reduce Ravage to 0 damage without any damage increases thus not bringing out any Infections. Grease Monkey and Pipe Wrench are good just because it offers more damage, never a bad thing. Pipe Wrench also reduces the damage Plague Rat will be dealing to Mister FIxer by 1, which can mean the difference between triggering Shadowy Ambush. Alternating Tiger Claw can be handy if Plague Rat plays his Bestial Vitality or gains any other DR from the environment. Rivieting Crane isn't bad to have in play if it's the only Style, as any hero before Mister Fixer in turn order will not have to worry about Bestial Vitiality or an environment providing DR for atleast 1 round, saving a Charge or Bloody Knuckles will allow the heroes to ignore it again for a second round. Grease Gun stops Plague Rat from dealing damage for a round, which can be much needed.

Note that the only Tool not mentioned is Tire Iron. Since the only target in Plague Rat's deck is Plague Locus, however Tire Iron may be useful in delivering the final blow to it. While not be specifically useful agianst Plague Rat himself, it may have a use taking out the ENvironment targets.
